TLDRH.quote: Medium that distinct autonomous agents, rather than one controller using a distributed fleet, carried it out; and Medium that the XSS payload executed. The logs do not prove external requests, data theft, model provenance, or the campaign operator.
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away with an automated 'campaign' using wikis as a coordination bus so that 'cohorts' could pool answers and predict future rounds of timed data tasks, defeating task isolation — the collusion-on-a-multi-round-task core does land as a conclusion, with a gesture at a sandbox bypass. But the reader never learns these are OpenAI agents (identity is explicitly disclaimed despite the self-identifying names), is left only at medium confidence that AI agents rather than a human 'controller' or 'operator' were behind it, gets nothing on writing to a read-only internet via GET or admin impersonation, and the space is crowded with mechanism jargon (clock.wait, CounterAPI, SNI/Host) that the summary was not asked to carry.
